Some comapnies are now spending as much on AI as human employees.

Gumroad is the latest to put a number on it, and the number is striking mostly because of how far it had to fall to get there. Founder and CEO Sahil Lavingia shared a chart this week showing Gumroad’s human payroll against its AI token spend going back to June 2021. In June 2021, the company spent $419K on W2 employees and contractors, and literally nothing on AI. That figure held roughly steady through 2022 at $406K, before beginning a steep decline: $258K in June 2023, $309K in June 2024 (a brief uptick), then $203K in June 2025. By June 2026, human payroll had fallen to $43K a month. AI token spend, meanwhile, crept up from $689 in 2023 to $5K in 2024, $13K in 2025, and finally $43K this June — matching payroll dollar for dollar for what Lavingia says is the first time.

The payroll collapse is the more dramatic line on the chart, and it lines up with what Gumroad has been saying publicly for over a year now.Gumroad had said in May last year that it would no longer hire senior or staff-level software engineers, a follow-up to an earlier freeze on junior and mid-level hiring announced that February.

A second chart posted alongside the payroll data shows just how concentrated Gumroad’s engineering output has become. A “top committers” graph puts AI at around 150 commits, dwarfing everyone else on the team, most of whom sit in the single digits. Read next to the payroll chart, it paints a picture of a company where AI is now doing most of the heavy lifting in writing code, and is only periodically assisted by humans on the team.

Customer support tells a similar story. Gumroad’s official account posted that its support SLA had dropped to 15 minutes, down from 24 hours earlier this year. Lavingia added that the team is currently averaging two minutes per response, a number that would have been unthinkable for a company running a traditional support desk. Gumroad’s had earlier made the case for moving away from hourly compensation altogether , with Lavingia arguing that AI-driven productivity gains of 5 to 20x make per-hour billing structurally irrational. The support response times look like an early proof point for that thesis.

None of this means Gumroad has stopped employing people. The company still spent $43K on payroll in June, and Lavingia has previously talked about keeping a small core team while pushing everyone toward AI-assisted workflows rather than eliminating headcount outright. What’s changed is the ratio, and the speed at which it changed. It took Gumroad roughly five years to cut payroll by nearly 90 percent, and about three years to build AI spend up from zero to match what’s left of it. If the trend lines from the chart continue in the same direction, AI token spend crossing over payroll entirely looks less like a hypothetical and more like a matter of a few months.

Gumroad has built something of a pattern out of these disclosures. Lavingia posts hiring freezes, token counts and productivity multiples on X the way other founders post revenue milestones. This latest chart fits the same mold: a small, remote-first team using its own operations as a live case study for how far AI can be pushed inside a real company, publicly, one metric at a time.
